Description.Summary: Mobile-Agent (also known as MobileAgent) is a computer-use / GUI automation agent family developed by Tongyi Lab at Alibaba Group. It autonomously operates mobile devices, desktop computers, and web browsers by perceiving the screen via screenshots and executing actions such as click, swipe, type, and scroll — all without requiring app-specific XML metadata or system APIs. The project spans multiple versions (v1 through v3.5) and is open-sourced under MIT license at github.com/X-PLUG/MobileAgent, with the underlying GUI-Owl model family available on Hugging Face and ModelScope. Deployment surfaces include a Python CLI run from a local machine with ADB (for mobile), pyautogui (for desktop), or Playwright (for browser), plus a cloud API on Alibaba's Bailian / Model Studio platform.

evidence.quote: Mobile-Agent: The Powerful GUI Agent Family
MobileAgent-v3 is a multi-modal and multi-platform GUI agent built upon GUI-Owl series models.
Mobile-Agent is an autonomous agent for mobile devices built on Multimodal Large Language Models. It uses visual perception tools to find and identify visual and text elements on an app's interface.

The primary language is Python.

Practices.Summary: Testing in Mobile-Agent is predominantly benchmark-driven evaluation rather than unit or integration testing. The team evaluates each model version against a suite of GUI agent benchmarks including AndroidWorld, OSWorld-Verified, ScreenSpot-Pro, WebArena, VisualWebArena, WebVoyager, and the team's own Mobile-Eval. Evaluation is run via shell scripts (e.g., run_guiowl15.sh, run_ma35.sh) with parameters set in script files. Some community contributors have proposed adding pure-Python unit tests for specific parsing functions (e.g., parse_action), though none were present in the main branch at the time of research.

evidence.quote: Evaluation apps and instructions are listed in English and Chinese, with privacy-sensitive details redacted.
Include pure-Python unit tests for the normal, empty, missing-tag, and bad-JSON cases.

Tools.Summary: The team uses AndroidWorld, OSWorld, ScreenSpot-Pro, WebArena, VisualWebArena, and WebVoyager as primary evaluation benchmarks. Inference is run via vLLM and Hugging Face Transformers. Android Debug Bridge (ADB) is used to execute actions on real Android devices during evaluation. The team also introduced Mobile-Eval, a custom benchmark covering 10 single-app and 1 multi-app scenario, for the original Mobile-Agent-v1 paper. Playwright is used for browser automation tasks in the browser_use submodule.

evidence.quote: Setting: Dynamic evaluation on real devices, with actions executed through Android Debug Bridge (ADB).
The Mobile-Eval benchmark covers 10 single-app scenarios and 1 multi-app scenario.
Browser and web benchmarks use a requirements.txt, a virtualenv, and playwright install chromium.

Stakeholders.Summary: Benchmark evaluation is performed by the research authors — primarily Tongyi Lab researchers at Alibaba Group. The community also participates by reproducing benchmarks and reporting discrepancies, as evidenced by issue #254 where an external contributor flagged a 3.9-point gap between the reported and reproducible ScreenSpot-Pro score.

evidence.quote: GUI-Owl-1.5-8B-Instruct scores 67.2% on ScreenSpot-Pro versus the reported 71.1%. A reproducibility gap.

Others.Summary: The training pipeline for GUI-Owl models includes a Step-Level Critic that labels each action as GOOD, NEUTRAL, or HARMFUL, and a Trajectory-Level Critic with both textual and multimodal channels — a trajectory is only counted as correct when both critics agree. This critic-based filtering acts as a quality gate on training data. The team also uses hint-guided rejection sampling and iterative online rejection sampling during data collection.

evidence.quote: A Step-Level Critic labels each action as GOOD, NEUTRAL, or HARMFUL. A Trajectory-Level Critic uses a textual channel and a multimodal channel, and a trajectory counts as correct only when both agree.

Practices.Summary: The repository has no formal CI/CD pipeline or automated test runner. There are no .github/workflows YAML files visible. Deployment is handled manually: contributors clone the repository, install dependencies via pip from requirements.txt, configure parameters in shell scripts, and run evaluation jobs manually. The team maintains cloud sandbox environments for training, using Android, Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows cloud phones/computers.

evidence.quote: Training environments run on cloud phones and cloud computers across Android, Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows.

Tools.Summary: Infrastructure tools include vLLM for serving models at inference time, Android Debug Bridge (ADB) for Android device control, pyautogui for desktop automation, Playwright for browser automation, and cloud sandboxes (Alibaba Cloud / Alibaba Mobile Use) for training and demo. Model weights are hosted on Hugging Face and ModelScope.

Others.Summary: The training infrastructure for GUI-Owl uses a rollout manager that assigns task IDs and coordinates data flow through a shared data center. Rollout is decoupled from policy updates, enabling fully synchronous or slightly off-policy asynchronous training for speed. The RL framework runs nearly 10,000 concurrent environments during the online RL stage.

Issues.Issue_Title: parse_action raises IndexError when model output is empty or lacks <tool_call>
Issues.Description: The parse_action function crashed with an unhandled IndexError when the model returned empty output or output without the expected <tool_call> XML tag, because the code used a bare string split without validating that a second element existed. A community contributor proposed adding regex-based extraction, retry logic with --max_parse_retries, and unit tests.

Issues.Issue_Title: Mobile-Agent-v3.5 image preprocessing uses factor=28 but GUI-Owl-1.5 (Qwen3-VL) may require factor=32
Issues.Description: A contributor identified a possible patch-size mismatch: the smart_resize call uses factor=28 (matching Qwen2.5-VL's 28x28 visual token blocks) but GUI-Owl-1.5 is built on Qwen3-VL which uses 32x32 blocks. Additionally, image encoding and coordinate rescaling use different factor values (28 and 16 respectively), which could cause coordinate drift in predicted click positions.

Issues.Issue_Title: Image size alignment in computer_use module uses inconsistent factor values (16 vs 28)
Issues.Description: Two smart_resize calls in the computer_use module used different factor values (16 in the runner, 28 in utils.py), introducing an approximately 1% image size error in coordinate scaling. Fixed by maintainer junyangwang0410 via commit 04f5e08.

Issues.Issue_Title: GUI-Owl-1.5-8B-Instruct reproducibility gap: 67.2% vs reported 71.1% on ScreenSpot-Pro
Issues.Description: A community contributor could not reproduce the 71.1% ScreenSpot-Pro grounding score reported in the technical report; their best result with the same hardware and preprocessing was 67.2%. The gap was traced to prompt template sensitivity — the correct evaluation prompt was not disclosed in the repository.

Issues.Issue_Title: _call_api function in browser_use/agent.py raises AttributeError accessing .text on message object
Issues.Description: Lines 119 and 121 of agent.py accessed a .text attribute that does not exist on the OpenAI message response object; the correct accessor is response.choices[0].message.content. Fixed by maintainer junyangwang0410 via commit c389195.

Issues.Issue_Title: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'OpenOCR' when running PC-Agent
Issues.Description: Users attempting to run PC-Agent fail with ModuleNotFoundError for the OpenOCR module. The setup README does not provide the correct installation method; pip-installing packages named 'openocr' and cloning the OpenOCR GitHub repository both fail. No maintainer response or resolution has been provided.

Issues.Issue_Title: PC-Agent config.py missing OCR_ACCESS_KEY_ID key causes KeyError at startup
Issues.Description: Running PC-Agent on macOS raised a KeyError for 'OCR_ACCESS_KEY_ID' because the configuration documentation did not list all required keys. Users had no complete reference for the config.py file.

Issues.Issue_Title: PC-Agent Windows installation fails: ModuleNotFoundError for tools.infer_e2e
Issues.Description: On Windows with Python 3.10, after following setup instructions, running run.py failed with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tools.infer_e2e'. The local OpenOCR folder inside PC-Agent conflicts with the installed openocr-python package, preventing the tools subpackage from resolving.

Issues.Issue_Title: GUI-Critic-Test image paths don't match evaluation JSONL — correct/incorrect labels reversed
Issues.Description: The evaluation JSONL and the images in the Hugging Face dataset zip archive were mismatched because the 'correct' and 'incorrect' subfolder labels were accidentally reversed during upload. Maintainer confirmed the Hugging Face dataset was updated after the issue was reported.

Issues.Issue_Title: Upstream version pinning: remotely downloaded resources break without version control
Issues.Description: A contributor reported recurring breakage because Git dependencies and remote model resources are downloaded without pinning to specific commit hashes or versions. Additionally, OS-specific requirements files (requirements_win_v1.txt, requirements_mac.txt) were incomplete and conflicted with the main requirements.txt.

Issues.Issue_Title: iic/GUI-Owl-1.5-32B-Instruct model produces consistently inaccurate coordinates
Issues.Description: A self-hosted deployment of GUI-Owl-1.5-32B-Instruct via vLLM produces coordinates that are off by a large margin, causing all agent actions to fail. The issue suggests the vLLM server configuration (tensor parallelism, tool-calling parser, or visual preprocessing) may interact incorrectly with the model's coordinate output format.

Issues.Issue_Title: Mobile-Agent-v3.5 agent cannot open system apps like Phone; failed click shows misleading install error
Issues.Description: The agent fails to recognize or open system applications such as the Phone app. When a click fails, the agent incorrectly interprets the response as an instruction to install the app, producing misleading error output instead of a useful diagnostic.

Practices.Summary: Bug resolution follows an informal GitHub Issues workflow: users report issues (often in Chinese), maintainers (primarily junyangwang0410 and zhangxi1997) triage and close them — often on the same day as a fix commit. Recurring engineering problem categories include: (1) image preprocessing inconsistencies (factor values, coordinate mapping); (2) dependency and environment configuration failures (OpenOCR, requirements file gaps, version pinning); (3) unhandled edge cases in output parsing (bare splits, missing XML tags, empty model output); (4) dataset/artifact mismatches (reversed folder labels, mismatched evaluation code); (5) benchmark reproducibility gaps (undisclosed prompt templates).

evidence.quote: junyangwang0410 committed a fix that references the issue (commit c389195). The issue was closed as completed on March 25, 2026.

Tools.Summary: GitHub Issues is the primary bug tracking system. There is no evidence of a dedicated issue tracking tool such as Jira or Linear. Debugging relies on user-provided error logs, stack traces, and screenshots shared directly in issue comments.

Stakeholders.Summary: Core maintainers junyangwang0410 (Junyang Wang) and zhangxi1997 (Xi Zhang), both Tongyi Lab researchers at Alibaba Group, handle the majority of bug triage and fixes. Community contributors also submit fixes via pull requests (e.g., Lendle-King, Kingpython123, vw2x).

Others.Summary: A systemic pattern is that the research team prioritizes releasing new model versions and benchmark results rapidly, sometimes leading to underdocumented configuration requirements, unpinned dependencies, and inconsistent preprocessing parameters across submodules. Many closed issues are resolved within hours to days, suggesting responsive but reactive (rather than proactive) quality assurance.

Practices.Summary: Mobile-Agent follows a research-driven, paper-first development model typical of academic AI labs. Each major release corresponds to an academic paper (ICLR 2024 Workshop for v1, NeurIPS 2024 for v2, preprints for v3 and v3.5). Development appears iterative: each version improves the agent architecture and training methodology incrementally, with formal evaluation against established benchmarks before release. The team does not appear to follow Scrum or Agile sprints; development cadence is tied to research milestones and paper submission deadlines.

evidence.quote: Mobile-Agent-v1 (ICLR 2024 Workshop); Mobile-Agent-v2 (NeurIPS 2024); UI-S1 (ACL 2026 main); GUI-Critic-R1 (NeurIPS 2025)

Tools.Summary: Development uses Python as the primary language with PyTorch for model training. The team uses a self-evolving data pipeline (automated query generation, rollout, critic filtering) and scalable RL frameworks (TRPO for v3, MRPO for v3.5). Git with GitHub is used for source control and collaboration.

evidence.quote: A self-evolving pipeline generates queries, rolls out trajectories, judges correctness, and produces guidance for hard queries.

Others.Summary: A notable documentation gap is that configuration requirements are sometimes incomplete, as illustrated by multiple issues where users could not find the required keys for config.py or the correct evaluation prompt templates. The team addresses these gaps reactively through issue responses rather than proactively updating documentation.

evidence.quote: The reporter asked for a complete configuration list for config.py, saying they were desperate for one.

Practices.Summary: Mobile-Agent integrates LLMs at multiple levels. Early versions (v1, v2) used GPT-4V via the OpenAI API for visual decision-making and GPT-4 (text-only) for planning. Later versions (v3, v3.5) replaced closed-source APIs with the team's own GUI-Owl model family (built on Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL). The multi-agent framework in v2 uses three separate LLM agents: a planning agent (text-only), a decision agent (multimodal), and a reflection agent (multimodal). Prompts for each agent are published in the academic paper appendix. The training methodology for GUI-Owl uses a hybrid approach: supervised fine-tuning on curated trajectories followed by reinforcement learning (TRPO, then MRPO) with accuracy rewards and format penalties.

evidence.quote: The planning agent (text-only GPT-4) condenses history into a pure-text task progress, so the decision agent doesn't have to read long interleaved image-text histories.
Prompts for each agent are published in the appendix, with separate initial and subsequent planning prompts.
The reward is an accuracy reward (1 for success, 0 otherwise) plus a format penalty of -0.5 for malformed actions.

Tools.Summary: LLM integration tools include: the OpenAI Python SDK (for GPT-4V API calls in early versions), Qwen-Agent library (qwen_agent Python package) for GUI-Owl-based agents, vLLM for serving GUI-Owl models at inference time, and Hugging Face Transformers for local model loading. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is natively supported by GUI-Owl-1.5 for tool calling.

evidence.quote: Python packages: qwen_agent, qwen_vl_utils, numpy
Native tool and MCP calling.

Stakeholders.Summary: LLM integration and prompt engineering is handled by the core research team. The GUI-Owl training pipeline — including data flywheel design, critic-based filtering, and RL reward design — is led by the Tongyi Lab researchers (Ming Yan, Haiyang Xu, Jiabo Ye, Xi Zhang, and collaborators).

evidence.quote: Jiabo Ye, Xi Zhang, and Haiyang Xu are marked as equal contributors. Ming Yan is the corresponding author and project leader.

Others.Summary: GUI-Owl-1.5 introduces unified thought synthesis that integrates world modeling, knowledge injection, and MCP reasoning into each training step. The training uses a self-evolving trajectory production framework where the model iteratively refines its own training data. GUI-Owl models output relative coordinates on a 0-1000 scale, and a community-identified bug (issue #285) suggests the coordinate system's factor parameter may be misconfigured relative to the Qwen3-VL tokenizer, illustrating the tight coupling between LLM tokenization and the agent's spatial reasoning.

evidence.quote: Unified CoT Synthesis: Integrates world modeling, knowledge injection, and tool/MCP (Model Context Protocol) reasoning into each step.
The models output relative coordinates on a 0-1000 scale by default.
